title: Early parades and phonograph music
summary: Allen asks about earliest music; Brunies recalls plain marches, mule-drawn floats and learning from phonograph records.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever use piano much in the early bands? Oh, yeah. I had a piano a lot of times. Yeah. Well, I don't want to bother you anymore. We've been having a nice talk here. I don't want to keep asking you a lot of questions. I can't think of much more. I can't think of much more, actually, to ask you. I wondered if there was any more about the early music, the very first that you heard the kind of parades, even when you were a boy, before you learned to play. Did they have the parades?
Carnival Parades. Did they ever play any ragtime in those days? No, just marches. Just plain marches.
And had a father behind ewes, didn't they?
The ewes used to pull the floats. Yes. And, uh, Irish bands, brass bands, marches. Yes.

And the very early dance music, when you were a little boy, even before you learned to dance or before you learned to play, can you remember any of the dance music you might have heard from outside of a ballroom or outside of a tavern, what kind of music they might have had?
No, it is from that record, from the phonographs. From the phonographs. Very early. It hit my head like that. Yeah. I'll play that.
And you knew it right away and you could play it right as soon as you heard it.
